complexity.notes: Correct but heavier than needed: the zero-handling branches, list slicing (which copies O(n) elements), and match/case add complexity versus the standard two-pass prefix/suffix approach, which also avoids division entirely. Division via // relies on exact divisibility and would break if division were disallowed, as the classic problem requires.
complexity.summary: Counts zeros and branches: with 2+ zeros all outputs are 0; with exactly 1 zero it computes the product of the non-zero elements and places it at the zero's position; with no zeros it computes the total product and divides by each element.
